Implement revocation handling (stop calling, delete the token) and the re-authorization recovery path

approval.cost: No submission or listing fee is stated anywhere in the docs read
approval.trigger: Review is the gate for external users: 'New Apps are available only to users in your App's Workspace. By default, external users can't install your App until it's approved and published in the Webflow Marketplace.' Pre-approval testing cap: 'Request to add up to 5 test users at support.webflow.com with their Webflow emails. Once added, share your app's install URL so they can try it out.' (Testing access 'is separate from creating a private app'.) Private apps are not an escape hatch: if the app is 'a custom app for a specific workspace or custom implementation, you can publish it as a private app and control who can install it... All private apps are reviewed just like public apps.' Submission process: prepare technical requirements and submission assets; submit via the Webflow App submission form; respond to feedback if needed; publicize upon approval and publication. Technical requirements include: two-factor authentication enabled for an admin account on the workspace; a thoroughly tested, fully functional app ('Marketplace apps should be complete, functional, and ready for their intended audience at submission. Apps that are beta, incomplete, or pre-release should not be published to the Marketplace'); clear documentation and error handling; and compliance with the Marketplace Guidelines. Reviewer requirements: complete reviewer access (demo account with full functionality, gated/premium feature access, test credentials, sample data) that 'must not expire during review'; backend services live throughout review; a demo video (2-5 minutes) that, for Data Clients, 'must also demonstrate a working OAuth flow for users approving and denying the request'; a published .webflow.io testing site with the app installed; for new apps and code/scope-changing updates, an App Review Preflight receipt (a changes_required result blocks submission); for Designer Extension/Hybrid apps, a review ZIP of source maps/build files. The form machine-checks the install URL: 'The client_id must match your Client ID, and the scope parameter must request only scopes you selected in the form.' After approval: approval covers the reviewed version/configuration/permissions; updates go through the same review process (submission type 'App Update'), including updates that change 'requested permissions'. 'If we hit a blocking issue, such as a failed installation or OAuth flow, we stop the review there and send you that feedback', and Webflow 'don't pre-review Apps, give advance approval, or check fixes outside the queue'. If changes are requested: 'fix every item, retest your App end to end, and resubmit'; 'Repeated submissions that don't fix earlier feedback can pause new submissions for your App.' Webflow may also run compliance audits post-approval.
approval.wait: 'We'll email you to confirm we received your submission, and we aim to send a decision within 10 business days' (stated as an aim, not an SLA)

blockers.detail: 'You cannot add new scopes; the scopes section of the App building blocks is locked after the App is published. If the App requires new scopes, you must go through the approval process again.' The documented workaround is to register a copy of the App to test new scopes, then submit an 'App Update' listing the new scopes; only after approval should you update your OAuth URL: 'Do not update the Webflow OAuth URL before the App update is approved... If you do, users see a scopes mismatch error that prevents them from authorizing the App.' After a scope change, 'the App prompts users to re-authorize'.
blockers.howToClear: Finalize the scope set before first submission; treat scope additions as a new approval cycle.
blockers.title: Scopes are locked after publication

blockers.detail: 'The scopes requested in your install or OAuth URL must be equal to or a subset of the scopes configured in your App's settings': requesting more fails installation; requesting fewer silently leaves API calls failing for missing scopes. Reviewers also 'will verify that requested scopes correspond to the functionality you advertise'; read-only apps must request :read scopes only, and custom_code:read / custom_code:write are 'treated as elevated-risk scopes' because they inject site-wide JavaScript.
blockers.howToClear: Request exactly the scopes the advertised functionality uses, no more.
blockers.title: Install-URL scopes must be a subset of configured scopes

blockers.detail: The official Webflow FAQ says, in the context of changed permissions, 'There is no way to refresh the App's access token or add scopes to it', and no refresh-token grant is described in the OAuth flow documentation read. The documented recovery paths are revocation and re-authorization.
blockers.howToClear: Design the connection lifecycle around re-authorization rather than refresh; confirm the token response against your own testing before assuming refresh exists.
blockers.title: No documented refresh path

tested: Read-only verification: the App/Data Client model, the external-user review gate, the 5-test-user cap, scope locking, and the 15-minute code rule were checked against developers.webflow.com (no app created, nothing submitted). Third-party tutorials describing Webflow token responses with refresh tokens were NOT relied on; Webflow's official docs read do not describe a refresh token, so that point is recorded under Unverified rather than asserted.
unverified: Access token lifetime/expiry (no numeric lifetime for OAuth access tokens is stated in the authentication, registration, or guidelines pages read).

Refresh tokens (no refresh-token grant, lifetime, or rotation behavior is described in the OAuth documentation read; the only official statements are the FAQ's 'no way to refresh the App's access token', in the permissions-change context, and the Guidelines' generic instruction to 'implement token refresh and expiry handling correctly'. Whether a refresh token is issued at code exchange is therefore not confirmed from official docs).
Fees (no Marketplace submission/listing fee or revenue share is stated in the docs read).
Whether the '10 business days' is a guarantee (the docs phrase it as an aim, not an SLA).
A hard cap on installs for an approved app (no per-app install/user ceiling is stated; the only numeric pre-approval cap found is the up-to-5 external test users).

The exact token-endpoint request/response schema (the authorize URL format and flow were confirmed from the submission/registration docs, but the OAuth token endpoint's reference page was not read in this pass, so its URL and response fields are not asserted).

alternatives: Site Tokens (per-site API tokens a site owner generates in Site Settings; suitable for first-party/single-site integrations where the site owner hands you a token; not a user-consent flow and not multi-tenant)

Workspace Tokens (Enterprise-only tokens created by workspace admins for workspace-level resources, e.g. audit logs; they 'don't have access to the site scope', so they can't substitute for site data access)
flavor.recommended: An App with the Data Client capability, running the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow against the Webflow Data API
flavor.why: The object is an App registered inside a Webflow Workspace (Workspace Settings > Apps & Integrations > App Development), assembled from 'building blocks': a Designer Extension (runs inside the Webflow Designer via the Designer API), a Data Client ('Data Clients can read and write site data and connect to third-party infrastructure with OAuth via the Webflow Data API', the OAuth-bearing block), or a Hybrid App (both). Webflow's Marketplace Guidelines are explicit: 'Webflow requires OAuth 2.0 for authenticating Apps. Do not collect Webflow credentials manually or implement workarounds that bypass the OAuth authorization flow.' During authorization the user chooses which sites (or their whole Workspace) to grant: registration offers an option to 'Restrict app installation to a specific site', so users 'can authorize your App for only a single site at a time', or by default 'authorize your App for multiple sites or their entire Workspace at once'.

humanMust: Meet the prerequisites: a Webflow account and a Workspace where you have Admin permissions ('Only Workspace admins can create Apps, view client secrets, upload bundles, and modify App settings'; email-verified account with 2-factor authentication; app development on Team and Enterprise plans)
Create the App and add details (name, description max 140 characters, icon, Homepage URL); optionally restrict installation to a specific site
Define building blocks and OAuth configuration: select the Data Client, select the OAuth scopes, add an HTTPS redirect URI; record the Client ID and Client Secret
Submit for Marketplace review with the full reviewer packet (demo account, demo video, testing site, Preflight receipt)
name: Webflow
nuances: OAuth flow security requirements (Marketplace Guidelines): a unique state parameter on EVERY authorization request, verified before code exchange; the redirect URI must EXACTLY match the registered URI (trailing slashes and localhost ports must match exactly: 'https://example.com/callback and https://example.com/callback/ are different URIs'). Token handling: tokens only in secure server-side storage (encrypted database/secrets manager), never browser local/session storage, plaintext, logs, or responses; the client_secret must never appear in client-side code or public repos.

Session semantics: signing out of your app 'must not invalidate the underlying Webflow authorization unless that is the explicit intent', and you must not re-trigger OAuth on routine logins/session events. Disconnect/uninstall behavior is reviewed: users must be able to fully revoke access; when a token is revoked your app must stop calling the API with it and delete it, and uninstalling must remove what your app added (including Custom Code at site and page level); revocation 'immediately invalidates' a token.
Identity guidance: use authorized_user:read / Get User Info endpoints for identity rather than broader scopes, and don't request workspace-level scopes when site-level suffices.

Authorization URL pattern: webflow.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<YOUR_CLIENT_ID>&scope=<SCOPES>; the recommended installation pattern goes straight to Webflow OAuth (or to your platform first and then into OAuth). Token introspection (Get User Info) confirms identity and what the token is authorized for.
prerequisites: A Webflow Workspace with Admin permissions (Team or Enterprise plan for app development)
An HTTPS redirect URI registered exactly
Server-side token storage (encrypted) ready before submission

steps.detail: Dashboard > select the Workspace > Settings > Apps & Integrations > App Development > Create an App. Add details: name, description (140 characters max), icon, Homepage URL (valid HTTPS link); optionally toggle 'Restrict app installation to a specific site'.
steps.title: Create the App in your Workspace

steps.detail: Select Designer Extension and/or Data Client; for a Data Client, select the OAuth scopes your App needs and add a redirect URI ('a valid HTTPS URL where users will be redirected after authorizing your app'). Click 'Create app'. The registered App shows its Client ID and Client Secret in the App Development section. Store access tokens server-side per connecting user (never in browser storage).
steps.title: Configure the Data Client (scopes, redirect URI)

steps.detail: Direct the user to webflow.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&scope=... with a unique state. The user chooses which sites (or their whole Workspace) to grant. Verify the returned state before exchanging the code, and use exactly the registered redirect URI. Codes 'are valid for 15 minutes and may only be used once. Exchange them for an access token immediately. Do not retry, persist, or log authorization codes.'
steps.title: Run the OAuth flow (15-minute single-use codes)

steps.detail: Call api.webflow.com/v2/... with Authorization: Bearer. Use the Get User Info / token introspection endpoints to confirm identity and what the token is authorized for. Tokens can be revoked programmatically or by users in the dashboard; on revocation, stop calling and delete the token.
steps.title: Call the Data API

steps.detail: Pre-approval, you may add up to 5 test users via support.webflow.com. To reach external users: prepare the technical requirements and submission assets, submit via the Webflow App submission form, and respond to feedback. Reviewer access must not expire during review; the demo video (2-5 minutes) must demonstrate a working OAuth flow for Data Clients; include a published .webflow.io testing site and an App Review Preflight receipt. 'We aim to send a decision within 10 business days.'
steps.title: Test (up to 5 users), then submit for Marketplace review

tagline: OAuth is mandatory and Marketplace review gates everyone outside your own Workspace (private apps are reviewed too, and only 5 test users are allowed before approval). Scopes lock permanently at publication, codes live 15 minutes, and Webflow's docs describe no refresh token at all.

time.active: ~20 min of app setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code + reviewer-packet preparation
time.total: About two weeks or more: decision aimed within 10 business days, plus resubmission cycles
time.waiting: Marketplace review: aim of a decision within 10 business days (stated)
